title: fix(e2e): use default temperature for Luna judge (#4053)
message: fix(e2e): use default temperature for Luna judge (#4053)
pr_body:
## Summary
- Remove the hardcoded `temperature: 0` from LLM judge requests while keeping `gpt-5.6-luna` as the default model.
- Add regression coverage for YES/NO evaluation against Luna's temperature constraint, model override precedence, and invalid verdict rejection.

## Root cause
The Luna Azure deployment rejects `temperature: 0` with HTTP 400 and supports only its default temperature. Omitting the parameter allows the same proxy/model to return a valid judge verdict.

This fixes the independently reproduced parameter compatibility issue. The HTML response parsing failures in [E2E run 38097949444](https://github.com/SerendipityOneInc/ecap-workspace/actions/runs/38097949444) remain unconfirmed: the live probe used proxy credentials, not the GitHub E2E secret.

## Test plan
- [x] Regression tests failed with HTTP 400 before the fix; all 3 pass after the fix.
- [x] ESLint and targeted TypeScript checks pass for both changed files.
- [x] Repository web governance guards pass.
- [x] Generate the request body from the modified judge and send it through `https://litellm.vllm.yesy.dev/v1/chat/completions`: HTTP 200 with `YES: The response correctly answers the question.`
- [ ] Full-project TypeScript check: blocked locally by shared-component type mismatches and missing dependencies (`yaml`, shared-package React types) while reusing the main checkout's node_modules. CI must verify the clean dependency installation.
- [ ] Full E2E run using the original CI credentials.

author: tim-srp
title: feat(claw-interface): let usage records read only the caller's own usage (#4052)
message: feat(claw-interface): let usage records read only the caller's own usage (#4052)
pr_body:
## Summary

`GET /users/credits/usage/records` scopes the read to the caller's current membership, so a **team org admin always gets the whole org** and has no way to read their own usage. This adds an optional `scope` query parameter to the existing endpoint: no new endpoint, and no change for existing callers.

| `scope` | Team org admin | Team org member | API key | No team org |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| omitted / `org` (default) | whole org, unchanged | own usage since joining, unchanged | unchanged | personal wallet, unchanged |
| `self` | **own usage since joining** (`user_id` + `visible_from=joined_at`, the filter billing-gateway already applies to members) | unchanged | unchanged (the key scope keeps precedence) | personal wallet, unchanged |

The response echoes the applied value in `meta.scope` (`"org"` or `"self"`). A caller can then tell this server from one that predates the parameter and silently ignores it. An unknown value is rejected with a 422 before any read.

Changes: `resolve_usage_scope(..., self_only=False)` in `app/services/billing_usage_access.py`, plus the query parameter and the `meta.scope` echo in `app/routes/credits.py`. The web callers (`organization-usage.ts`, `billing.ts`, `enterprise-admin`) send no `scope`, so their behaviour is unchanged.

**Consumer:** the ecap-workforce "my usage" page, where admins and members read their own usage the same way.

## Tests

- `test_billing_usage_access.py`
  - `self_only` filters an admin and a member to the caller.
  - An API key scope is unaffected.
  - A personal wallet is unaffected.
- `test_user_credits.py` (through the ASGI route)
  - Default and `scope=org` keep the org total for an admin.
  - `scope=self` narrows the read to the admin.
  - A member is unchanged.
  - `meta.scope` is echoed.
  - `scope=member` is rejected with a 422 before any read.
- Three existing mocks of `query_billing_usage` now return a `meta` like the real one does. The function already rejects a body without `meta`.
- The new tests fail on `main` and pass on this branch.
- Locally:
  - ruff, ruff format, `pyright app/ tests/` (0 errors), lint-imports, and the file-length and complexity guards are all clean.
  - Full `tests/unit`: 11913 passed and 14 failed. All 14 failures are in `tests/unit/test_admin_cron.py` (`'_IncludedRouter' object has no attribute 'path'`, a local venv incompatibility). The same 14 fail on the untouched base, so they are not caused by this change.

## Verified against real staging data (not deployed)

staging runs `staging-194efc7`, the base of this branch. I ran this branch's route locally, with its storage reads answered by staging's API for the caller and billing-gateway reached through a read-only port-forward. For each of the 24h, 7d and 30d windows on a test team org:

- **Default path:** this branch's answer equals staging's answer exactly (totals, every bucket, every model, display names) for the admin and both members.
- **`scope=self` for the admin:** the answer is the admin's own usage. It matches billing-gateway queried directly with the admin's `user_id` and `joined_at`: 15 credits and 1 LLM call, against an org total of 66.
- **`scope=self` for members:** the answer is identical to what staging already returns them.

Nothing was deployed; this PR does not touch any environment.
